title: ‘This idea that we can now eat our clothes is pretty revolutionary’: how to give unwanted garments a second life

paragraphs.english: This page is an independently written reading guide to an article by Petra Stock in The Guardian, first published online on 20 February 2026 in the paper’s Change by degrees series on household sustainability. The original text is available at the link below.
paragraphs.chinese: 本页是为 Petra Stock 发表在《卫报》上的一篇文章独立撰写的阅读导读，文章于 2026 年 2 月 20 日首次在线发布，属于该报关于家庭可持续生活的“Change by degrees”系列；原文见下方链接。

paragraphs.english: The article begins with a piece of furniture almost every reader owns: a wardrobe that will not close. Australians are buying more new and second-hand clothing than ever, and the surplus has to go somewhere. The question the piece sets out to answer is practical rather than philosophical — what should a household actually do with the garments nobody wears any more?
paragraphs.chinese: 文章从一件几乎每个读者家里都有的家具写起：一个关不上的衣柜。澳大利亚人购买的新衣和二手衣都创下新高，多出来的东西总得有去处。文章要回答的问题偏实际操作而非哲学思辨——家里那些再没人穿的衣服，究竟该怎么处理？

paragraphs.english: The numbers come first. A report by Seamless, the country’s clothing stewardship scheme, found that about 1.5 billion new garments were bought nationally in a single year, the equivalent of fifty-five items for every person. Of the clothes that are discarded, roughly half go straight to landfill, a little under four in ten are reused locally or exported, and under one in ten are recycled. The landfill share works out at some 229,000 tonnes a year.
paragraphs.chinese: 先看数字。澳大利亚的服装责任计划 Seamless 的一份报告发现，全国一年购入约 15 亿件新衣，相当于人均 55 件。在最终被丢弃的衣物中，大约一半直接进填埋场，接近四成的衣物在当地再利用或出口，被回收的不到一成。进填埋场的那部分折算下来约为每年 22.9 万吨。

paragraphs.english: Ainsley Simpson, Seamless’s chief executive, supplies the frame for those figures. She describes the overconsumption of clothing as having become normalised, and argues that this has already locked in a climate and water footprint out of step with any circular future: around 14.5 million tonnes of carbon emissions and the equivalent of 1.8 billion tonnes of water. Notice the move being made here. What looks like a private matter of crowded cupboards is being restated as an industrial balance sheet.
paragraphs.chinese: Ainsley Simpson 是 Seamless 的首席执行官，她为这些数字提供了理解框架。她认为，对衣物的过度消费已经变得“正常化”，而这已经锁定了一笔与循环未来并不匹配的气候与水足迹：约 1450 万吨碳排放，以及相当于 18 亿吨水的消耗。注意这里完成的转换：一件看似私人的事——塞满的衣柜——被重新表述成了一份产业账本。

paragraphs.english: The middle of the article turns to a single New Zealand label, Kowtow, which has spent years stripping plastic and petrochemicals out of its production. The point is that this goes well beyond the fabric. Zips, buttons and even the polycotton thread were either designed out or replaced with recyclable or natural alternatives, so that a garment can be described as genuinely plastic-free.
paragraphs.chinese: 文章的中段转向一个新西兰品牌 Kowtow，它花了好几年把塑料和石化材料从生产中剔除。关键在于，这件事远不止于面料：拉链、纽扣，甚至混纺涤棉线，要么在设计阶段就被去掉，要么换成了可回收或天然材料，这样一件衣服才谈得上真正的无塑料。

paragraphs.english: That thoroughness only makes sense once you see what the company wants to do at the end of a garment’s life. Kowtow has begun turning its textile waste into biochar — a charcoal made from organic material that can be used to enrich soils. The scheme has so far converted a tonne of what would otherwise have been waste, and the founder, Gosia Piatek, describes mixing it with soil to grow tomatoes in the label’s own workroom. Hence the strange phrase in the headline about eating one’s clothes.
paragraphs.chinese: 只有看清这家公司想如何处理衣服的生命终点，这种彻底才有意义。Kowtow 已开始把纺织废料做成生物炭——一种由有机材料制成的炭，可用来改良土壤。该方案至今已把一吨本该成为垃圾的织物转化掉；创始人 Gosia Piatek 说，他们把这个和土拌在一起，在自家工作室里种番茄。标题里“吃自己的衣服”这个古怪说法就是这么来的。

paragraphs.english: The loop closes neatly. Returned items have their trims removed and fed back into the repair programme, so repair and recycling are treated as one system rather than two competing services. Tessa Bradley, the label’s head of sustainability, sums up the intention: by unmaking what has been made, the company gives something back, and the end of a garment becomes the beginning of something else.
paragraphs.chinese: 这个闭环合得很整齐。被送回的衣服会拆下配件，重新投入修补计划，于是修补与回收被当成同一套系统，而不是两项互相竞争的服务。品牌可持续发展负责人 Tessa Bradley 概括了这层用意：通过把做出来的东西再拆解，公司回馈了些什么，一件衣服的终点也就成了另一件事的起点。

paragraphs.english: Set against that, the article offers a picture of ordinary confusion. Seamless estimates that 5.27 billion items are stockpiled in Australian wardrobes, which is 193 pieces for every person in the country. A survey led by RMIT found that most people owned clothes they had not worn for a year, and that a third had not touched half of what they owned.
paragraphs.chinese: 与之对照，文章给出了普通人困惑的一面。据 Seamless 估算，澳大利亚人的衣柜里积压着 52.7 亿件衣物，等于全国人均 193 件。RMIT 主导的一项调查发现，多数人拥有整整一年没穿过的衣服，三分之一的人有半柜衣物从未动过。

paragraphs.english: Simpson’s advice is a ladder rather than a single step: re-wear, repair and share where possible, and donate good-quality items to established charity and resale networks, which extends their life and reduces demand for new clothing. The charity sector adds a test of its own. Matt McMahon of Salvos Stores suggests that if an item is good enough to give to a friend, it is probably good enough to donate — a reminder that donation is not a disposal route for rubbish.
paragraphs.chinese: Simpson 的建议是一把梯子而非单一动作：尽量重复穿着、修补和分享，并把品质尚好的衣物捐给成熟的慈善与转售网络，从而延长使用寿命、减少对新衣的需求。慈善行业自己又加了一道标准。Salvos Stores 的 Matt McMahon 提出，如果一件东西好到能送给朋友，大概也就好到可以捐赠——这提醒人们，捐赠不是垃圾的处理渠道。

paragraphs.english: The recycling end of the ladder is the weakest. Textiles have the lowest recycling rate of any waste material, at about five per cent, and most of that is carpet rather than clothing; federal data put textile waste at roughly 33 kilograms per person, with garments the largest component. Tailored schemes remain niche, which is why the article spends time on the exceptions.
paragraphs.chinese: 这把梯子最弱的一环在回收端。纺织品的回收率是所有废弃物中最低的，约为百分之五，而且其中大部分是地毯而非衣物；联邦数据显示，人均纺织废弃物约 33 公斤，其中衣物占最大比重。专门的回收方案仍然很小众，这也是文章要花篇幅讲例外案例的原因。

paragraphs.english: In South Australia, state and local governments worked with charity partners on statewide collection drives that accepted clothing, footwear and linens in any condition; a single event recovered almost 20 tonnes of unwanted textiles for resale and recycling. Seamless is also funding pilots, including postal return satchels run with Australia Post and RM Williams, workplace collections, charitable collaborations and local recycling hubs.
paragraphs.chinese: 在南澳大利亚，州政府、地方政府与慈善伙伴合作开展全州范围的收集活动，接受任何状态的衣物、鞋履和床品；仅一场活动就回收了近 20 吨待转售或回收的旧纺织品。Seamless 还在资助若干试点，包括与 Australia Post 和 RM Williams 合作的邮寄回收袋、办公场所收集点、与慈善机构的合作以及本地回收站。

paragraphs.english: The final section widens the lens again. Julie Boulton, a sustainable fashion consultant, argues that the idea of clothes as disposable items has to go, and that the fix is system-wide: producers should be responsible for what they put on the market, and damaging materials should not be used in the first place. She also points at volume — much of what is made is heavily discounted or left unsold, with the true cost of production written out of the price. Her advice to shoppers is deliberately modest: buy what you need rather than what you want, and do not buy on impulse.
paragraphs.chinese: 最后一节又把视野拉宽。可持续时尚顾问 Julie Boulton 认为，“衣服是一次性用品”这个观念必须去掉，解决办法是系统性的：生产者应对自己投放市场的东西负责，有环境危害的材料根本就不该使用。她还指向数量问题——被生产出来的东西有大量被打到很低折扣或卖不出去，而生产的真实成本被从价格里抹掉了。她对消费者的建议刻意克制：买你需要的，而不是你想要的；不要冲动购物。

paragraphs.english: It is worth noticing what the article does not claim. A single tonne of biochar is a demonstration, not an industry, and the label behind it is one company among thousands. Recycling, on the evidence given, cannot absorb the volume now being produced. The piece therefore holds two arguments at once — that households should handle their own clothes better, and that better handling will not be enough on its own — without pretending to rank them.
paragraphs.chinese: 值得注意的是文章没有主张什么。一吨生物炭只是示范，谈不上产业，做这件事的品牌也只是千百家公司中的一家。就文中给出的证据看，回收无法消化当前的产量。因此这篇文章同时握着两个论点——家庭应该更好地处理自己的旧衣，而仅靠更好的处理并不够——并且不去假装给它们排序。

paragraphs.english: Here is an editor-written practice sentence, not a quotation from the original article: Even if every household sorted, repaired and donated its unwanted clothing perfectly, the volumes described in this report suggest that collection schemes alone could not keep pace with the rate at which new garments arrive in wardrobes.
paragraphs.chinese: 下面是一句编辑自拟的练习句，并非原文引用：即便每个家庭都把不要的衣服完美地分拣、修补和捐出，本报告描述的数量也说明，仅靠收集方案跟不上新衣进入衣柜的速度。

paragraphs.english: As you read, watch how the argument is assembled: national statistics, then one company’s experiment, then expert quotation, then policy. Keep the middle terms of that sequence separate — reused, donated and recycled are not interchangeable, and the article’s numbers depend on the distinction. Note also the small verbs of obligation and possibility (“should”, “could”, “suggest”), which mark where the writer is reporting a case and where she is arguing one.
paragraphs.chinese: 阅读时请留意论证是如何搭起来的：全国统计数字，然后一家公司的实验，再是专家引语，最后是政策。请把这条链条中间的几个词分开——再利用、捐赠和回收并不等价，文中的数字正依赖这一区分。另外注意那些表示义务与可能性的小词（should、could、suggest），它们标出了作者在哪里转述案例、在哪里提出主张。

sentenceNotes.sentence: What looks like a private matter of crowded cupboards is being restated as an industrial balance sheet.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: 主句为 What looks like a private matter of crowded cupboards is being restated as an industrial balance sheet：主语是 What 引导的名词性从句，谓语为 is being restated（现在进行时被动），as an industrial balance sheet 作主语补足语。
sentenceNotes.structure: What looks like... 是主语从句，looks like 意为“看起来像”；of crowded cupboards 修饰 a private matter。主句用被动进行时，突出“被重新表述”这一动作，而动作的施予者被省略。
sentenceNotes.translation: 一件看似私人的事——塞满的衣柜——正被重新表述为一份产业账本。
sentenceNotes.tip: balance sheet 是会计术语“资产负债表”，此处引申为“要算总账的东西”。注意 restate 的 re- 表示“换一种说法再说一遍”，不是“再次声明”；这句是作者的评论句，用主语从句让批评显得克制。

sentenceNotes.sentence: Textiles have the lowest recycling rate of any waste material, at about five per cent, and most of that is carpet rather than clothing; federal data put textile waste at roughly 33 kilograms per person, with garments the largest component.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: 由分号连接的两个并列分句：一是 Textiles have the lowest recycling rate...；二是 federal data put textile waste at roughly 33 kilograms per person。
sentenceNotes.structure: at about five per cent 是插入说明，解释 rate；most of that 中的 that 指前面那 5% 的回收量。rather than 表取舍对照“而不是”。分号后 put X at Y 是“把 X 估计为 Y”的搭配；with garments the largest component 是 with 复合结构，作补充说明。
sentenceNotes.translation: 纺织品的回收率是所有废弃物中最低的，约为百分之五，而且其中大部分是地毯而非衣物；联邦数据显示，人均纺织废弃物约为 33 公斤，其中衣物占最大比重。
sentenceNotes.tip: most of that 指“那 5% 的回收物”，不是“5% 这个比率”，读错会得出相反结论。rather than 前后是同类项对比；with + 名词 + 形容词是英语压缩信息的常用手段，翻译时展开成“其中……”。

sentenceNotes.sentence: Even if every household sorted, repaired and donated its unwanted clothing perfectly, the volumes described in this report suggest that collection schemes alone could not keep pace with the rate at which new garments arrive in wardrobes.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: 主句为 the volumes suggest that...：主语 the volumes，谓语 suggest，that 引导宾语从句 collection schemes alone could not keep pace with the rate...。
sentenceNotes.structure: Even if 引导让步状语从句，表“即便”，从句用一般过去时表假设；described in this report 是过去分词短语后置修饰 volumes；at which new garments arrive in wardrobes 是“介词 + which”引导的定语从句，修饰 the rate。
sentenceNotes.translation: 即便每个家庭都把不要的衣服完美地分拣、修补和捐出，本报告描述的数量也说明，仅靠收集方案也跟不上新衣进入衣柜的速度。
sentenceNotes.tip: 这句是本站编辑自拟的练习句，不是原文引用，只用于练习结构。keep pace with 意为“跟上……的步伐”，宾语是 rate；collection schemes alone 中的 alone 放在名词后表示“仅仅、单靠”，位置一变意思就变。Even if 假设未定之事，even though 则承认既成事实。
